chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Abu Wallad al-Hannat, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Ali ibn Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) used to say: 'The recognition of the completion of the religion of a Muslim is his leaving speech in what does not concern him, and his scarcity of quibbling, and his forbearance, and his patience, and his excellence of manners.'
ai.seo_question: What are the signs of a complete Muslim's religion according to Imam Ali (AS)?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Al-Kafi, Imam Ali ibn Al-Husayn (Zayn al-Abidin) outlines the ethical markers of a true believer (al-Mu'min), emphasizing that spiritual perfection is manifested through social conduct and self-restraint. This teaching aligns with the Shia emphasis on 'Akhlaq' (character) as the outward expression of 'Iman' (faith), highlighting that silence, patience, and good manners are not merely virtues but essential components of religious completeness.
